absent: Numeric ABI values for capacity scale, load frequency, migration cost, nice limits, priority mapping, and bandwidth shifts.
Runtime enqueue, dequeue, pick, preemption, wakeup, migration, and load-balancing behavior beyond initialization.
Root domain and scheduling domain construction, reference lifetime, and attach semantics.
Bandwidth enforcement, throttling, period handling, and cross-processor unthrottle processing.
Extension scheduler enablement, dispatch selection, sub-scheduler handling, and watchdog recovery actions.
Pressure averaging formulas, trigger thresholds, notification delivery, and cgroup integration.
Runqueue locking hierarchy, interrupt state requirements, and memory ordering guarantees.
Task group creation, full layout, online handling, and realtime group teardown internals.

findings.text: Boot scheduler initialization provides validated class ordering, prepared wait and group and domain and bandwidth state, default-configured runqueues for every possible processor, established initial weight and idle thread on the boot processor, started fair and extension and pressure and clamp and preemption support, and scheduler marked as running.
Required class precedence is stop above deadline above realtime above fair above idle, with extension ordered between fair and idle when that configuration is present.

A boot-configured runqueue carries zero running count, cleared load tracking, idle fallback selection, detached domain pointers, full capacity, cleared balancing and online state, initialized task list, attached root domain, and prepared masks, timing, polling and server helpers.

A newly initialized deadline runqueue is empty with no earliest deadline, cleared overload indication, zeroed local bandwidth use, empty cached tree roots, and ratio state derived from global realtime limits.
Deadline bandwidth ratio denotes full capacity when global realtime runtime is unbounded and otherwise denotes a scaled share derived from runtime and period.
Deadline server binding associates a server entity with its runqueue and its task selection callback for later scheduling use.
Fair and extension servers each start from an initialized embedded deadline entity bound to the local runqueue with their respective selection routine.
Fair class initialization provides per-processor balancing masks, throttling cross-call structures where configured, scheduling soft interrupt handling, and idle polling bookkeeping.

Extension class initialization provides per-processor dispatch queues, runnable and deferred lists, synchronization, inter-processor work, online marking, operator reset and dump hooks, and watchdog work.
Extension class setup has dual availability with full per-processor and global preparation when enabled and no operation otherwise.
A dispatch queue carries an identity and owner, prepared lock and list, and per-processor extensions each linked back to the queue with deferred requeue linkage prepared.
Idle tracking comprises global masks, per-node masks sized for noncontiguous nodes, and per-processor local and cache-level and NUMA masks.
Rescue support has dual availability with a dedicated queue plus pinned timer and termination timestamp when enabled and no operation otherwise.
Pressure stall initialization honors global and cgroup enable controls, establishes a sampling period, and prepares the system group, leaving monitoring disabled when globally disabled.

A pressure group carries enable state, averaging window and lock, average triggers with counts and deferred work, polling triggers with lock and list, polling period limits, wakeup queue, timer, and polling task pointer.
The default root domain holds a single reference after base initialization.
Every bit-wait table entry starts prepared as an empty wait queue.

Sleeping-context diagnostics report blocking attempts outside running state or with mismatched preemption and read-copy-update nesting, disabled interrupts, idle context, nonblocking sections, corrupted stacks, or held locks, with rate limiting and boot and shutdown exclusions.

Atomic-context and non-migratable-context diagnostics emit rate-limited reports when atomic or migration-disabled context is wrongly assumed, suppressed when interrupts are disabled or expected nesting already holds.

Nice update enforces range validity, serializes against concurrent scheduling, preserves realtime and deadline priorities while recording the static value, and otherwise refreshes weight and recomputes normal and effective priorities.
Effective priority retains an existing realtime or deadline priority and otherwise adopts the computed normal priority derived from policy, realtime level, and static value.
Scheduling statistic storage is conditional on enablement in one configuration and a no-operation in the other.

Normalization walks all threads under task-list protection, skips kernel threads, clears execution and waiting accounting, restores negative user nice values, and converts realtime and deadline user tasks to normal policy.
The current-task accessor returns the task presently assigned to the named processor.
A dedicated spinlock exists for task group bookkeeping.
Fair teardown synchronizes leaf-list removal under runqueue lock, removal accounting under interrupt-safe protection, and throttled-work draining under interrupt-safe protection.
Task group release unregisters fair and realtime portions and then defers final release through a read-copy-update grace period before freeing.
Fair group unregistration releases bandwidth control, detaches load averages for present entities, and removes queued runqueues from leaf tracking.
Entity load removal synchronizes blocked average against last update time and then folds utilization, load, and runnable averages into removal counters.
Bandwidth destruction is a no-operation when bandwidth was never initialized and otherwise cancels timers and drains pending throttling cross-call work across processors.
